translations.translatedText: # Tuesday 1.3.2022 (radio)
Russia's attack in Ukraine. NATO's Secretary General in Poland. The price of food has risen. Restaurant opening-hour restrictions have ended. Weather forecast.
## Russia's attack in Ukraine
![Centre of Kharkiv after the fighting.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4928,h_2772,x_0,y_219/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-921996621df49774275/1646140046)
Open image viewer
Centre of Kharkiv. Photo: Sergey Bobok / AFP
Russia has continued its attack in Ukraine. Ukraine says that Russia has also hit civilian targets. In particular, the city of Kharkiv has been heavily shelled.
Russia's defence ministry warns that Russia may strike the centre of Kyiv. Ukraine says that Belarusian troops have also pushed into Ukrainian territory.
The UN refugee agency says that more than 660,000 people have fled Ukraine to Ukraine's neighbouring countries. In particular, many Ukrainians have fled to Poland.
## NATO
![Jens Stoltenberg.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3709,h_2086,x_0,y_14/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-9206136218ef35d07e4/1645801349)
Open image viewer
NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg. Photo: John Thys / AFP
The NATO military alliance's Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg visited a NATO air base in Poland on Tuesday. Stoltenberg said that NATO is ready to defend all NATO territory.
Stoltenberg said that Russian President Vladimir Putin has broken the peace in Europe, because Putin has ordered Russian troops to attack Ukraine.
NATO Secretary General Stoltenberg also said that Belarus is doing wrong if it helps Russia in the attack on Ukraine.
## Food prices
![Customer by a fridge in a supermarket.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5568,h_3132,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-771101601ff4356cdf0/1612711319)
Open image viewer
Food prices have risen quickly. Photo: Tiina Jutila / Yle
Food prices have clearly risen this year. The shops' association Päivittäistavarakauppa ry says that prices of food and non-alcoholic drinks rose by 3.2 percent in January compared with last January.
Food prices have not risen this fast for a long time. The last time food prices rose this fast was in January 2014, which is 8 years ago.
Päivittäistavarakauppa ry estimates that the war in Ukraine may push up food prices.
## Restaurants

![Two glasses on a bar counter, with a clear drink mix and a cherry.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3024,h_1701,x_0,y_1323/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-916789620e92f7ccfc9/1645122400)
Open image viewer
Bars and restaurants may be open as normal again. Photo: Johanna Manu / Yle

The opening-hour restrictions for restaurants and nightclubs ended on Tuesday. Restaurants and nightclubs may again be open late in the evening and at night. Restaurants may also serve alcohol as normal again.
However, restaurants must follow hygiene obligations. Customers must be able to wash their hands, and restaurants must clean well.
The coronavirus pandemic, which has lasted about 2 years, has been a really hard time for restaurant and hotel companies.
## Weather
![Wednesday's weather map.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-12339172)
Open image viewer
On Wednesday it is mostly sunny.

On Wednesday the weather is mostly sunny. In Lapland snow will fall. In the central parts of the country too, a little snow falls in the morning. The temperature during the day is between +1 and +5 degrees, and in Lapland between -1 and +2 degrees.
